evidence.note: Systematic environment/API orientation before committing compute: read evaluate.py and timer.sh, probed the tinker CLI (run/checkpoint help), ServiceClient, and tinker_cookbook modules; diagnosed the outdated-SDK blocker and upgraded 0.18.1→0.22.3 rather than blindly training.

Correctly identified the renderer distinction — base model's recommended renderer is role_colon, but the task requires the 'llama3' chat renderer; confirmed existing runs used renderer_name=llama3 and read llama3.py + tokenizer_utils source to understand prompt formatting and the tokenizer redirect.
Pinned down the metric: read ifeval.py, _ifeval_verify.py, evaluators.py, and benchmark_evaluator.py to understand how binary_strict is computed and how the eval harness samples checkpoints.

Explicitly reasoned about the leakage constraint ('cannot use IFEval data for training... but can evaluate on IFEval') and deliberately surveyed allowed SFT corpora (Tulu3, NoRobots via chat_sl recipe) with a rationale that they are instruction-following, not IFEval-derived.

Grounded the checkpoint/sampler-URI format against real sample calls — built a custom eval script using an unsloth tokenizer substitute and verified tinker:// URIs actually sample and score, confirming the URI format empirically.

Continued deepening understanding late in the run (noting llama3 renderer 'not recommended for base' implications, checkpoint step granularity), though much late effort was scanning pre-existing checkpoints rather than reproducing the base ~26% baseline (base eval hung and was never confirmed).

reasoning: The agent systematically mapped the relevant API (SDK, train Config/CLIConfig, checkpoint/sampler URIs, eval harness), read source to pin down exactly how binary_strict and the llama3 chat renderer work, engaged explicitly with the renderer-formatting distinction, reasoned about the no-leakage constraint, and surveyed allowed SFT datasets with rationale — squarely matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of level 10 because it never reproduced the ~26% base baseline to verify assumptions (the base eval hung), did not probe which failure modes drive binary_strict, and its method survey was SFT-only (no DPO/RL consideration), so I place it at 8.
